newsitem.title: USA: Human tests to start on flu pill.
newsitem.headline: Human tests to start on flu pill.

text.p: Human tests will start early this year on a drug researchers hope will eliminate that scourge of winter, the flu, drug researchers said on Tuesday.
Preliminary tests on several animal species show the compound, known as GS 4104, is effective both in preventing influenza and treating it once someone gets sick.

Although the drug developers from Gilead Sciences Inc. held a Washington news conference to describe their high hopes based on animal studies, extensive testing must be done to establish that it is safe and effective in people.
It could take a few years to complete clinical trials and get regulatory approval.

"We think it will give people a new option for the control of influenza infection," Gilead scientist Norbert Bischofberger said. "All of you have had it at least once, and all of you will probably get it again."

The scientists outlined a scenario in which people could take a pill once or twice a day to ward off the virus during the flu season, which lasts six to eight weeks. Alternatively, the drug could be used by people who know they have been exposed, at an office or a daycare centre for instance, or when they start getting flu symptoms.
The compound works against varied strains of the flu but not against the virus that causes the common cold. It works in a novel way, targeting an enzyme the virus needs to reproduce.

For the young and healthy, influenza is usually just an unpleasant way to spend a few days, but in elderly people or people with other health problems it can be fatal. An epidemic of a virulent strain killed about 20 million people in 1918.
According to data cited by Gilead it is also responsible for about 15 million days of missed work a year in the United States alone.

Gilead, which has presented some of this data at earlier science meetings, announced last year that it had an agreement with Hoffmann-LaRoche, a branch of Roche Holding Ltd., to develop and commercialize GS 4104.
